idea-plugin.name: Vernac
idea-plugin.description:
Domain-Driven Design for Java, expressed in Vernac.

Vernac is a domain-specific language for defining typed identifiers, value objects, entities, aggregates, events, repositories, ports, services, and use cases. Its compiler generates Java code following consistent architectural conventions, while custom business logic remains Java.

Create your first project

Select New Project → Vernac to create a Maven project with a small domain model and a Java test. Choose your project name, Maven coordinates, Java package, and a registered JDK with Java 21 or newer.

  • Ready-to-build project template with Maven Wrapper
  • Consistent package declarations, imports, and source paths
  • Automatic Maven import
  • Automatic opening of the initial Vernac model
  • Project-specific README with build instructions

Editor features

  • Automatic recognition of .vernac files
  • Semantic highlighting
  • Syntax and semantic diagnostics
  • Code completion and snippets
  • Hover documentation
  • Go to Declaration for definitions within Vernac
  • New Namespace creates the Vernac directory structure
  • New Vernac File derives its namespace automatically from the selected directory

Language server and code generation

Open a .vernac file to activate language support. The language server is bundled and starts automatically. No separate language server installation or LSP4IJ configuration is required.

Java source generation runs through the Vernac Maven plugin. Projects created by the wizard already include its configuration. For existing projects, add the Maven plugin to your build.

Vernac build dependencies

Projects created by this plugin use Vernac @project.version@. Published release artifacts are downloaded automatically from Maven Central.

If the version ends in -SNAPSHOT, install the matching Vernac artifacts in your local Maven repository before building the generated project. Follow the Vernac repository build instructions.

The bundled language server provides editor support; Maven resolves the compiler and runtime dependencies separately.

The starter example requires no database, Docker, or running Spring application. Internet access is needed for the initial download of Maven and dependencies.

Project status

Vernac is under active development. Language syntax and generated APIs may change between releases.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
Inline Java behavior — first integration

  • Added Java language injection for inline behavior method bodies.
  • Private helpers share a Java context; method declarations retain Vernac source positions.
  • Uses the compiler's namespace/import rules and includes unsaved model changes.
  • Generate the domain Java sources first for receiver and model API resolution.

Project-wide type assistance

  • Type and import completion use namespace visibility across Vernac files.
  • Go to Declaration follows resolved type references and explicit imports.
  • Unsaved edits are included; ambiguous names have no arbitrary navigation target.
  • Grouped namespace/file actions near the top of New and hid duplicate generic template entries.

Namespace creation

  • Added New → Vernac Namespace with namespace-name validation.
  • New → Vernac File now derives the namespace from its target directory.
  • Updated file templates to the namespace syntax and an ID/VO example.

0.1.0-dev.3 — Project creation

  • Added the New Project → Vernac wizard.
  • Added editable Maven coordinates and Java package.
  • Added selection of registered JDKs with Java 21 or newer.
  • Included a Maven Wrapper, sample domain model, and Java test.
  • Added automatic Maven import and initial model opening.
  • Added a project-specific README.
  • Added template preflight checks and project generation tests.

Earlier development versions — Editor integration

  • Registered the Vernac language and file type.
  • Bundled the language server with automatic startup.
  • Connected editor features through the IntelliJ LSP API.
  • Added Vernac file templates.
